::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">Prairieland's energy minister asks for a pathway to 2050 for its five regions, and for its defence: what it costs, what it emits against the carbon budget, how secure it is, who pays, and what it means for Ridge County.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Also: how the pathway holds up against a gas-price spike, a drought, a mineral export restriction and a demand surprise.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a pathway link and a two-page policy brief, with the shock table as its sensitivity and the uncertainty that would change your recommendation; the Modeler version adds M13's notebook run on your pathway (its section 8).</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the <a href="sb4-pathway-explorer.html">Pathway Explorer</a>'s engine, its costs and fuels within their fixed ranges, and lesson <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a>'s accounting layer for who pays and for jobs (Prairieland is fictional; its numbers are illustrative).</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every check under the brief is in place, and the self-check reaches Proficient on every competence.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 240 minutes: 80 to build and test pathways, 40 to read the shocks, security, affordability and jobs, 80 to write the brief, 40 to check it.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Modeler version: plus <a href="m13-national-pathway.html">M13</a>'s notebook, about 60 minutes: set your pathway's levers in its section 8.</p>
</div>
```
:::

## Write your two-page policy brief
:::

```{=html}
<div id="c4-note" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c4-note:start -->
<ol class="lx-rn-outline"><li><b>Title and plan link:</b> the plan's link from the bench, and the date</li><li><b>Recommendation:</b> Three or four sentences: the pathway Prairieland should take to 2050, and why.</li><li><b>The plan:</b> each choice, with its unit</li><li><b>Results:</b> each result, with its unit and boundary</li><li><b>Assumptions:</b> one sentence each</li><li><b>Sensitivity:</b> how one result moves when one input changes, and whether the plan was held fixed</li><li><b>Cost, carbon and security:</b> Two or three sentences: the cost, CO₂ against the budget, imports against the cap.</li><li><b>Shocks and what would change the recommendation:</b> Two or three sentences: what the four shocks did, and which result would make you choose differently.</li><li><b>Who pays, and Ridge County:</b> Two or three sentences: households (a screening estimate, with your share and design) and Ridge County's jobs, gross and net.</li><li><b>Sources and credit:</b> One or two sentences: the data behind your numbers (EIA, IPCC, SPP through EIA-930; the course's teaching settings) and any conflict of interest.</li><li><b>Limits of this analysis:</b> what the model leaves out</li></ol>
<!-- c4-note:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

Imports, the strait, the peak hours: name the measure and the shocks.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> Jobs lost and gained, gross and net, with the coefficients stated.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong brief · Proficient</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Recommendation:</b> follow the central pathway: build 72.0 GW of wind, 32.5 GW of solar and 35.5 GW of gas by 2050, and widen links by 8.9 GW [1].
<b>Cost and carbon:</b> $401.6 billion to 2050 (present value, 2025 dollars, supply side and every fuel); CO₂ 3,600 of 3,600 Mt [2].
<b>Security:</b> imports at most 32% of primary energy against a 40% cap [3].
<b>Shocks:</b> Against four shocks re-planned from their year (the plan's builds up to it kept), the cost to 2050 moves by $0.0 billion to +$26.5 billion, most for the demand surprise; the budget is met under all four; imports stay within the cap; the peak-hour rule is short in the shock's year under drought and demand surprise. [4]
<b>Who pays (screening):</b> about $−130 a household a year in 2050 if households pay 50%; equipment not counted [5].
<b>Ridge County (screening):</b> 5,533 jobs lost against 1,152 new ongoing jobs (922 net) [6].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> Every lever with its size.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> One boundary, the budget's arithmetic stated.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> A measure and its limit.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> All four, with the rule for what was kept, as a range.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> A screening estimate with its share and what it leaves out.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> Gross and net kept apart; the multiplier and displacement stated.</li></ol></div>
